scoutingFocus: Young leaves and stem base
precautions: Observe seedlings regularly and maintain field sanitation
todayPriority: Establish a uniform and healthy seedling stand.
recommendedActions: Assess germination percentage and perform gap filling within 10 days of sowing
Monitor the soil moisture levels to prevent waterlogging around tender roots
Inspect the stem base for early fungal rotting or seedling collapse
Remove weeds manually to reduce early resource competition

scoutingFocus: Upper canopy and underside of leaves
precautions: Avoid excess nitrogen and inspect lower leaves
todayPriority: Promote robust structural canopy development.
recommendedActions: Apply recommended nitrogenous fertilizers in split doses to avoid succulent growth
Conduct inter-cultivation and mechanical weeding to keep fields clean
Inspect the undersides of top leaves for early sucking insect clusters
Uproot and safely bury stray plants showing severe leaf crumpling symptoms

scoutingFocus: Flowers, squares and young bolls
precautions: Inspect for rosette flowers and boll damage
todayPriority: Protect early squares and flowers to maximize fruit set.
recommendedActions: Install pheromone traps across the field to track adult moth arrivals
Examine open flowers daily for a twisted rosette appearance
Check the lower dense canopy leaves for whitish or grey powdery patches
Maintain stable soil moisture conditions to prevent stress-induced flower drop

scoutingFocus: Developing bolls
precautions: Monitor boll opening and internal damage
todayPriority: Defend developing green bolls and optimize fiber quality.
recommendedActions: Perform random destructive sampling of green bolls to check for internal burrowing
Monitor mature leaves for defoliation caused by fungal mildew progression
Regulate late-stage irrigations to encourage natural boll opening and drying
Pick cleanly opened bolls sequentially to prevent soil staining

scoutingFocus: Tender leaves
precautions: Maintain healthy nursery conditions
todayPriority: Nurture vigorous and pathogen-free seedlings.
recommendedActions: Keep nursery beds covered with a fine nylon net to exclude vector insects
Practice regulated, light watering cycles to avoid bed saturation
Apply bio-agents like Trichoderma to the nursery soil bed profile
Sort and discard weak, stunted, or pale seedlings prior to uprooting

scoutingFocus: Tender shoots and upper leaves
precautions: Inspect leaf curling symptoms
todayPriority: Establish crop architecture and monitor vector activity.
recommendedActions: Erect yellow and blue sticky traps right above the crop canopy height
Observe structural leaf deformation to separate upward and downward curling
Uproot and deeply bury field plants exhibiting clear mosaic or stunting signs
Provide balanced micro-nutrition to enhance early plant structural strength

scoutingFocus: Flowers and buds
precautions: Monitor flower drop
todayPriority: Safeguard flower retention and early pod formation.
recommendedActions: Gently tap flower clusters over a clean white surface to assess active insect load
Inspect the growing tips and twigs for water-soaked necrotic drying symptoms
Maintain uniform soil moisture levels to minimize physical flower shedding
Clean out channel boundaries to ensure efficient drainage of excess water

scoutingFocus: Flowers and fruits
precautions: Inspect fruits regularly
todayPriority: Protect mature pods from rot and bore damage.
recommendedActions: Examine developing green and red pods for circular, sunken necrotic spots
Check fruits for neat entry holes or larval boring marks near the calyx
Collect all rotten, dropped, or insect-damaged fruits from the field rows
Initiate picking of ripe, mature chillies during clear, dry daylight hours

scoutingFocus: Stem base and young leaves
precautions: Observe seedling establishment
todayPriority: Achieve high seedling survival and healthy root zones.
recommendedActions: Count emerged seedlings along rows to identify gaps requiring attention
Examine the soil-line collar area of wilting seedlings for dark lesions
Check loose soil around isolated wilting patches for root-chewing grubs
Execute early shallow hoeing to keep field lines completely weed-free

scoutingFocus: Leaf surface
precautions: Monitor leaf damage
todayPriority: Build a dense, clean vegetative canopy layer.
recommendedActions: Scan leaflets for clear, blister-like tunnels or internal mining tracks
Look out for scraped leaf surfaces or early caterpillar egg clusters
Complete the final deep inter-cultivation before the crop begins pegging
Check the lowest leaf tier for small, premature chlorotic spots

scoutingFocus: Canopy and pegging zone
precautions: Monitor humidity-related symptoms
todayPriority: Ensure unhindered peg entry into the soil matrix.
recommendedActions: Cease all mechanical hoeing or inter-cultivation to protect downward pegs
Inspect the foliage canopy for distinct circular brown spots with yellow halos
Keep the topsoil loose and moderately moist to aid easy peg penetration
Set up light traps at the field periphery to capture active adult moths

scoutingFocus: Canopy and root zone
precautions: Inspect defoliation symptoms
todayPriority: Prevent early defoliation to maximize pod weight.
recommendedActions: Check lower leaf layers for dark, halo-less lesions underneath the foliage
Evaluate total leaf drop levels to monitor overall plant stamina
Uproot a few sample plants at random to check pod shell hardening
Maintain moisture availability during the final critical pod-filling phase

scoutingFocus: Central whorl and tiny pinholes on young leaves
precautions: Apply seed treatment with Cyantraniliprole; remove alternate grass hosts near field borders.
todayPriority: Defend young emerging leaf whorls from early insect damage.
recommendedActions: Examine emerging central leaf whorls daily for tiny pinhole patterns
Look along the leaf surface for cream-colored, fuzzy insect egg masses
Clear out wild perennial grasses around the field perimeter boundaries
Document the overall field emergence pattern and calculate plant density

scoutingFocus: Whorl damage, fecal matter chunks, and long boat-shaped lesions on lower leaves
precautions: Whorl application of sand mixed with lime or poison baits if Fall Armyworm passes economic threshold.
todayPriority: Protect the vegetative canopy and control whorl feeding.
recommendedActions: Check growing whorls for ragged leaf damage and coarse sawdust-like frass
Drop dry sand mixed with lime directly into whorls to create a physical barrier
Scan mature lower leaves for elongated, straw-colored, boat-shaped lesions
Apply the recommended dose of nitrogen fertilizer followed by earthing-up operations

scoutingFocus: Tassel emergence, silk strings, and purplish-brown lesions on leaf sheaths
precautions: Ensure zero waterlogging; strip the lower infected leaves to break fungal contact with soil.
todayPriority: Secure clean tassel emergence and healthy silk development.
recommendedActions: Inspect emerging tassels and fresh silk strings for sticky insect colonies
Examine lower stalk leaf sheaths for distinct purplish-brown concentric bands
Manually strip off the lowermost infected leaves to halt fungal movement
Keep drainage furrows completely clear to prevent standing field water

scoutingFocus: Cob tips and stalk stability close to the ground line
precautions: Avoid moisture stress at grain filling to prevent charcoal rot; harvest immediately when black layer forms on grain base.
todayPriority: Ensure grain maturity validation and protect stalk integrity.
recommendedActions: Check cob tips for entry holes, larval boring, or mold development
Push stalks gently at the base to evaluate internal rotting or lodging risk
Maintain adequate root zone moisture until the late grain-filling phase wraps up
Peel back husks to verify the black layer formation at the kernel base

scoutingFocus: Stem base for water-soaked lesions and young leaves for curling
precautions: Ensure deep summer ploughing; treat seeds with Trichoderma viride or Metalaxyl to protect against damp soils.
todayPriority: Protect early seedling stems from fungal collar infections.
recommendedActions: Monitor the soil-line stem base for dark, water-soaked necrotic lesions
Check young leaf margins for yellowing or upward curling tendencies
Clear field drainage channels to prevent moisture accumulation near root crowns
Perform gap filling promptly to preserve target row spacing populations

scoutingFocus: Sudden wilting of patches or branches; webbing behavior on leaf axils
precautions: Rogue out wilt-infected plants immediately; maintain proper inter-row spacing to minimize microclimate humidity.
todayPriority: Monitor branch structural integrity and field wilt patches.
recommendedActions: Identify patches showing sudden foliage drooping and inspect for internal stem browning
Examine leaf axils and terminal shoots for early silk-webbing behavior
Run regular inter-row cultivation to keep the soil surface airy and clean
Nip the primary terminal buds on old plants to stimulate lateral canopy expansion

scoutingFocus: Flower clusters for drop or chewing damage; mosaic symptoms (pale green leaves with no flowers)
precautions: Install pheromone traps @5 per hectare; spray acaricides early to eliminate the mite vectors spreading sterility mosaic.
todayPriority: Maximize flower retention and monitor canopy discoloration.
recommendedActions: Fix pheromone traps just above the crop canopy line across the field
Gently shake flower clusters over a collection cloth to check for larvae
Scout for patches of pale green, bushy foliage devoid of flower buds
Ensure steady soil moisture status to prevent physical bud dropping stress

scoutingFocus: Bored holes on pods and internal seed damage; premature drying of whole plants
precautions: Monitor pod wall surfaces for tiny egg punctures; ensure need-based systematic insecticide applications before pods harden.
todayPriority: Protect maturing pods from internal seed-feeding pests.
recommendedActions: Look closely at the green pod walls for tiny pinpoint egg entry punctures
Check individual pods for clean, round exit holes or localized discoloration
Monitor older plants for rapid, premature drying out linked to root rot
Collect and clear away infested fallen pods to restrict pest cycles

scoutingFocus: Cotyledons and lower leaf margins for hopperburn (yellowing and downward curling)
precautions: Sow resistant varieties like Kranthi or Jyothi; treat seeds with Carbendazim to protect against soil pathogens.
todayPriority: Protect early cotyledons and secure uniform crop establishment.
recommendedActions: Check large cotyledon leaves for water-soaked reddish-brown circular spots
Inspect the outer margins of first true leaves for downward curling or yellowing
Maintain a loose, well-drained topsoil structure around the seedling stems
Thin out weak companion plants to maintain exact recommended single stand counts

scoutingFocus: Defoliation lines on lower leaves and sudden drooping/drying of upper foliage
precautions: Hand-pick semi-looper larvae in early stages; introduce bird perches throughout the field to promote natural predators.
todayPriority: Manage leaf-defoliating caterpillars and monitor stalk health.
recommendedActions: Inspect the lower canopy leaves daily for clean-cut chewing or defoliation lines
Install tall, sturdy wooden bird perches evenly across the field grid
Identify plants showing sudden leaf drooping or dark streaks along the stem
Conduct shallow hoeing between rows to expose soil-dwelling pest pupae

scoutingFocus: Developing spikes and individual flower structures for grey woolly fungal growth
precautions: Crucial stage during cyclonic rain windows in AP; immediately spray Carbendazim if continuous drizzle or high humidity strikes during flowering.
todayPriority: Safeguard emerging flower spikes from destructive grey mold.
recommendedActions: Examine developing flower spikes for soft, water-soaked tissue or grey woolly mold
Look for blackish frass or silk webbing around individual capsule joints
Ensure proper air circulation within the field rows by keeping weeds completely down
Prune away any heavily rotted individual spike tips to isolate healthy structures

scoutingFocus: Capsules showing internal frass or browning; concentric spots on top canopy leaves
precautions: Perform sequential picking of matured spikes (racemes) as they dry out to safeguard oil quality and prevent capsule shattering.
todayPriority: Execute timely sequential harvesting of mature, dry spikes.
recommendedActions: Check maturing capsules for boreholes, internal frass, or premature drying
Scan upper canopy leaf surfaces for dark, concentric ring blight spots
Harvest fully dried main spikes manually to prevent capsule field shattering
Examine the bases of late-forming spikes for white, sticky insect clusters
